actions.text: I put on the Garvey signet and make my way to the formal welcome dinner. At the doorway I pause to find the seating arrangement and see who is already there, then step inside rather than waiting to be announced.

"I wasn't sure whether I was supposed to knock, bow, or wait for someone to find me," I admit. "Walking in seemed the least likely to leave me outside until breakfast." I give her a small bow. "Rowan. Is there a place I'm meant to sit, or is choosing it my first examination?"

I take the indicated chair. "Then thank you for saving me from my first diplomatic incident." I set my hands on the table instead of hiding the ink stains. "I've spent the afternoon in a house that seems to be holding its breath. I'd rather hear about the people here than the seating rules. What do you all do when nobody is grading you?"

"Mostly stories. I give imaginary people better lines than I ever manage for myself." I glance down at my fingers, then back at Ashara. "Occasionally letters. Garvey House isn't much of a correspondent." I turn to Rashid, leaving the question open to him rather than making Ashara speak for the table. "What about you? What would you do with one afternoon that belonged entirely to you?"

"That sounds painfully familiar." I let the joke drop for a moment. "Come to Garvey House tomorrow afternoon, if you want. No audience and no assessment. We can discover whether either of us knows how to waste an hour." I look back to Ashara. "You're invited too. Though I'm not promising anything worth studying."

"Tomorrow, then." I lift my glass toward the rest of the table as well. "To learning something about each other that isn't already written beside our names." I take a drink, settle back, and listen as the welcome dinner continues, giving the others room to speak instead of filling every silence myself.

I glance along the quiet table, then address Caelindra with a tentative smile. "Is dinner always this solemn? I'm beginning to suspect Ashara is the only one allowed to answer." I tilt my glass toward Ashara so the teasing isn't hidden from her. "Or have I simply asked very dull questions?"

"Then I'll risk a concession first. I'm relieved to have a home, and frightened that it belongs to a dead family more than it belongs to me." I lower my glass and address Caelindra without the teasing. "What do you miss about yours? Not the court or the advantages. Something small you wish you could have brought with you."

"Then I won't ask you to defend it to me." I finish my dinner without pressing Caelindra for another answer. When I am ready to leave the table, I say quietly to her, "I'm going to take some air before I turn in. You're welcome to walk with me, and you don't owe me a conversation." I wait for her answer rather than assuming she will come.

I nod goodnight to the table and walk with Caelindra out of the dining room toward the Academy grounds. I leave comfortable space between us and, for the first few minutes, actually keep the silence I offered. I take in the night air and look for a quiet path or a place to sit, without leading us into any closed or forbidden area.

I stop at the next junction and take a proper look around, trying to orient myself. What lies along the open paths, and is there a bench or another clearly public place where Caelindra and I can sit? I am looking for something specific in the grounds, not trying any closed doors.

I take the terrace path and sit at one end of the stone bench, leaving room for Caelindra if she wants it. For a while I just watch the storm beneath us. "I've spent all evening trying not to look overwhelmed," I say at last. "I think I'll give that up for a minute." I let myself enjoy the view without asking anything of her.

"Thank you. For the company, and for that." I stay a little longer to watch the storm, then wish Caelindra goodnight without asking her to come farther. I return to Garvey House, go to bed, and sleep until morning unless something wakes me.

actions.text: I let the rest of the night pass, continuing to sleep until morning unless I am disturbed.

I get up and spend the morning making one common room in Garvey House feel inhabited: opening the curtains, dusting a table, and arranging three comfortable chairs. By early afternoon I set out tea and something simple to eat. I wait there for Rashid and Ashara's promised visit, ready to answer the door if either of them arrives.
